case_title: JAGTAR SINGH v. STATE OF HARYANA
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304 Part II read with s.34
aggravating_circumstances: Land dispute, motive existed prior to the crime, aggressor, caused fatal injuries
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.304 Part II read with s.34, sentenced to 5 years imprisonment and fine of Rs.1000/-
high_court_outcome: Upheld conviction of appellant, acquitted co-accused
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused and his brother had a land dispute with the victim. The accused and his brother approached the victim to reverse a land exchange they had previously made. During the confrontation, the accused caught hold of the victim's uncle, pulled him down, and hit him on the head, causing him to become unconscious and later die. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts and documentary evidence to establish the accused's involvement. The trial court and High Court found the accused guilty based on the evidence, while the co-accused was acquitted. The accused was sentenced to five years of imprisonment and a fine of Rs.1000/-.
